rationale:
bugs_open/254 — the indexed COMMIT becomes answer-site vocabulary, because the header banner was measured insufficient. THE INCIDENT: a landmine-verifier verdict explained the absence of ValueDef (a struct; three siblings from the same file indexed at that moment) as 'of kinds not indexed'. The symbol was absent because its commit had not been PUSHED — analyse_repo_local fetches the remote tarball, and the index sat 246 commits / 88 changed .go files behind the working tree. Proven both ways: after the owner pushed and the index refreshed, the SAME entry flipped NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW -> STILL_VALID with the indexed commit the only variable.

WHY THIS IS A PLACEMENT FIX, NOT A NEW GUARD. A 090 round (520b2f7e) refuted the naive diagnosis: freshnessBanner (87d0bcf97, bugs_closed/108 defect A) ALREADY renders the indexed commit, ref, age and 'local unpushed work is never visible' on every run, and an llm_call_log census proves that text was in all four verify-step prompts of the incident window (prompt_rendered LIKE '%never visible%' -> t on 4/4; the loud '%INVISIBLE below%' STALE branch -> f on 4/4, because codeIndexCommitStaleAfter=48h and the indexed commit was ~17h old by wall clock). The model QUOTED the kind census that phase 1 renders beside the empty answer and talked past the header a screen above. Two mechanisms in series: (1) the STALE branch measures wall-clock age, but staleness on a commits-outpace-pushes tree is commit DISTANCE, which the pod cannot measure (no checkout) — no threshold fixes an incident that happened at 17h; (2) the vocabulary available AT the answer wins — which is this file's own stated rule ('the distinction has to travel WITH the data', codeIndexScope doc comment), applied by phase 1 to kinds and extensions and never to commits.

THE CHANGE, all additive prose on existing seams: the one freshness query's result is threaded into codeIndexScope (as a loadCodeIndexScope PARAMETER, so forgetting to thread it is a compile error, not a silent degrade); every in-scope 0-row answer gains one as-of line naming the commit, ref and ABSOLUTE minute-precision commit time (the motivating gap was same-day: index at 16:27, symbol committed 23:13) and blocking the three wrong readings by name; codeEvidenceLine — the line append_doc_note suffixes onto every persisted verdict — now ends 'Answers describe indexed commit <sha> ... — the last pushed tip, not the present tree', so a doc_notes verdict can finally be dated against the code months later. The runtime lane threads the same struct through the same helpers (one judgement, no sibling copy). No new return keys, no schema change, no workflow change, no threshold change; the 48h branches keep their jobs (refresh-pipeline death, wall-clock age).

TESTING, mutation-first (a mutation survived this file's helper-only tests once — WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-10): the wiring test goes through answerCodeCheck for all three arms' empty answers, and both unwiring mutations (silencing the emptyAnswer append; silencing the evidence-line clause) were RUN and each fails its test. Full actions package green. Known limit, stated rather than hidden: the action-body threading (passing the real freshness struct rather than a zero value) is enforced by the signature, not by an action-level test — a deliberate zero-value pass would compile; it would also be visible in any review of the call site.

plan.summary: Date every empty code-index answer and every persisted evidence line with the indexed commit, threaded from the existing freshness query — because the header banner stating the same fact was measured read-but-unused in the motivating misverdict.

edits.rationale: One query, two renderings: the function already reads the high-water mark for the banner; it now also returns the struct so the answer-site renderings can reuse the SAME read rather than a sibling query that drifts.

The scope struct carries the freshness it was loaded alongside, as a PARAMETER of loadCodeIndexScope rather than a field a caller may forget to set — a forgotten assignment would silently reproduce the header-only state this bug is about.

The remedy proper: every in-scope 0-row answer carries the commit it describes, beside the kind/extension censuses the model demonstrably reads there. NOT gated on the 48h clock (the incident happened at 17h); absolute minute-precision date because ages are only true at render time and the motivating gap was same-day. Degrades to nothing when freshness is unreadable or the index empty (the banner branches already shout those), and to an explicit UNRECORDED line for pre-migration rows.

The persisted half: append_doc_note suffixes this line onto every landmine-verifier verdict, and before this change nothing the run persisted recorded which commit the answers described — a verdict read months later could not be dated against the code at all. Gated only on having read a commit: a failed freshness read loses the clause, not the line.

The runtime lane adopts the same threading through the same helpers — one judgement, not a sibling copy that drifts (016b §9). Its verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain acts on absence, so it needs the as-of vocabulary at least as much as the council tier.

grounded_in: llm_call_log census, incident window 2026-08-11 09:30–10:40Z, step_name IN ('verify','derive_checks'): all four verify rows have prompt_rendered LIKE '%index freshness%' -> t AND '%never visible%' -> t AND '%INVISIBLE below%' -> f. The caveat was present and the STALE banner was not.

The wrong verdict, doc_notes 2026-08-11 ~10:00Z: ValueDef/valueDefs '... are of kinds not indexed' — while code_symbols held FileInfo, FuncDef, TypeDef (struct) from the same file internal/analysis/types.go, and ValueDef is a struct.
The both-ways flip (lane NOTES, 08-11): same entry, re-verified after the push-triggered re-index — NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW -> STILL_VALID, 2 NOT ANSWERABLE -> 0, indexed commit the only variable.
diagnose_code_lookup_action.go:87-98: const codeIndexStaleAfter = 48h; const codeIndexCommitStaleAfter = 48h — the incident's indexed commit was ~17.5h old, so the FRESH branch rendered.
Distance measured at the incident: index at 5a68d6caf while the working tree was 246 commits and 88 changed .go files ahead (was 228 ninety minutes earlier — the gap grows while you read it).

codeIndexScope doc comment (same file): 'the prompt that tells a reviewer to treat the two differently is NOT in front of them when they read the result. So the distinction has to travel WITH the data.' — the rule this change extends from kinds/extensions to commits.

landmine-verifier default_config workflow: verify and verify_unverifiable steps reference results_text (banner included); persist_verdict references evidence_line (no commit text before this change). The wiring theory is refuted; the READ failed, not the compute or the wire.

090 round 520b2f7e (work item 3382da26, completed 2026-08-11 13:18Z): UNVERIFIABLE with last-hypothesis refuting the filed premise and naming the llm_call_log census as the deciding check — which is the census quoted above. First-hand substitution declared per the owner ruling of 2026-07-31.

bugs_closed/108 relation: its fix (pin to the live working branch) works and is untouched; 254 is the residual it leaves on a tree where commits outpace pushes — 'current with the branch' and 'current with the code' are different claims.

Mutation evidence, run 2026-08-11: silencing 'return base + s.indexedAsOfNote()' fails TestEmptyAnswersCarryTheIndexedCommit; silencing the evidence-line clause fails TestCodeEvidenceLineNamesTheIndexedCommit; restored file passes the full actions package.
plan.risks: 1. PROMPT GROWTH: one extra line (~340 chars) per in-scope empty answer, on runs capped at max_checks=8 — worst case ~2.7KB per lookup rendering; the evidence-line clause adds ~120 chars to each persisted doc_note. No cap or truncation seam is near these sizes. 2. A note that always prints can stop being read — the file's own principle. Accepted deliberately and stated in the doc comment: the note prints only on EMPTY answers (not all answers), and the alternative (clock-gating) is precisely what failed at 17h. If fleet evidence later shows the note being ignored, the next move is placement/wording, not removal. 3. The as-of note could be read as licensing 'it's just stale' hand-waving on symbols that genuinely never existed — mitigated by wording: the note names the postdating condition explicitly and the honest-absence sentence still renders beside it (asserted by TestLsArmKeepsHonestAbsenceForAnIndexedExtension, unchanged). 4. Signature changes are compile-contained: both callers of codeIndexFreshness/loadCodeIndexScope are in this change; go build ./... clean; no live agent_definitions reference either symbol (they are Go-internal, not action names).
